confirmed.suspectedCause: Two separate losses: (1) inline links dropped or moved out of plain paragraphs; (2) whole paragraphs dropped. Some of the dropped ones are the 2nd and 3rd paragraphs of h3 subsections that became cards (only the first paragraph is kept, cut at about 320 characters). The others ('Flour is grain…', 'Calcium propanoate…') are ordinary section paragraphs; the cause was not isolated.
confirmed.suggestedFix:
Never drop or truncate paragraphs in article scope. Keep inline links inside the sentence. Add a regression check that compares the 4-word shingle coverage of original

text against Sift text.
confirmed.verdict:
Reran the shingle check on live Bread in my tab: the same 7 paragraphs come back, and Sift's HTML has '

Dough recipes commonly call for 500 (about 1.1 pounds) of flour, which yields a single loaf of bread or two .

'. I found the cause of the first loss. Wikipedia now serves Parsoid HTML, where elements have ids like mwAdA, mwAdE, mwAdI and mwAds. tokens() in src/content/dom.ts:271 kebab-cases camelCase ids ('mw-ad-a', 'mw-ads'), and AD_TOKEN matches 'ad'/'ads', so isAd() drops them. In the page, exactly 8 elements match: a#mwAdA 'grams', a#mwAdE 'baguettes', p#mwAdI 'Calcium propanoate…', p#mwAds 'Flour is grain ground…' and their children. The other dropped paragraphs ('straight dough', 'Sourdough breads…', 'peasant families', 'Pressure-Vacuum', 'baker's yeast…') are the 2nd and 3rd paragraphs of h3 subsections that became truncated cards (see finding 14).
confirmed.fix: In tokens(), do not camelCase-split ids, or skip ids that match Parsoid's /^mw[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ before testing AD_TOKEN. Separately, do not turn h3+p runs inside the article into cards (finding 14).

confirmed.title: Released-for-fullscreen portals never come back when fullscreen does not happen (Ctrl+F, double click on controls, failed request)
confirmed.evidence: `addEventListener("keydown", (e) => releaseFor(e, () => key === "f" || key === "F", "video"), true)` has no modifier check, and dblclick releases for any target in a video portal. releaseForFullscreen sets `p.released = true`; the only reset is `if (!fs) p.released = false` in onFullscreen, and layout skips released portals (`if (parked || p.released) continue;`). In media('fullscreen'), `requestFullscreen?.().catch(() => layout())` calls layout() but layout still skips the released portal. setMode/checkUrl/setPortals never clear `released`, and the Portal object survives SPA navigation while the element is the same.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning from code: on YouTube in Sift, click the video (focus goes inside #movie_player), press Ctrl+F to search the page. keydown key is 'f' -> portal released, no fullscreen -> the player is no longer shown in its box, on this and every following video page until something enters and exits fullscreen. Same after double-clicking the next button or the seek bar.
confirmed.suspectedCause: Release is done optimistically and has no timeout or failure path.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Ignore 'f' with ctrlKey/metaKey/altKey. After releasing, check after about 500 ms (or on the next fullscreenchange/fullscreenerror) and, if document.fullscreenElement is not the element or an ancestor, set released=false and schedule layout. In the catch at index.ts:618, clear released too (export a 'cancelRelease(ref)').
confirmed.verdict: Read portal.ts:50-53, 155-161, 214-222 and 243-247. The keydown release tests only key==='f'/'F', with no modifier check. dblclick releases for any target inside a video portal. releaseForFullscreen sets released=true, and the only reset is in onFullscreen when fullscreenElement is null. layout() skips released portals, and media('fullscreen')'s catch(() => layout()) cannot bring the portal back. Nothing in setPortals, setMode or checkUrl clears the flag, and refs are stable per element (registry WeakMap). So Ctrl+F, Alt+F, or a quick double click on play/pause or skip inside the player leaves a black box until something enters and then exits fullscreen.
confirmed.fix: Release on 'f' only with no Ctrl/Meta/Alt and when the target is not editable. Release on dblclick only when the target is the video surface, not a control. After any release, if no fullscreenchange arrives within about 1 s (or requestFullscreen rejects), set p.released=false and call schedule().

confirmed.title: Enter/submit replays do not follow the browser's implicit submission rules (wrong button clicked, or a native submit where the browser does nothing)
confirmed.evidence: Default button: `Array.from(f.elements).find((e) => (e instanceof HTMLButtonElement && e.type === "submit" && !e.disabled) || ...)` skips a disabled first submit button and clicks the next one. Chrome does not submit when the default button is disabled (verified t10.ts: Enter in a form with <button disabled>Save</button><button>Delete</button> -> no submit). With no submit button, Sift calls f.requestSubmit(); Chrome does not submit when the form has 2+ text fields (verified t10.ts: user + password fields, no submit button -> no submit). Also: `f.checkValidity()` runs even when the form has `novalidate`, and the `button` path (172-175) skips the validity check entirely, so Chrome's own validation silently blocks the click (the invalid field is inert and cannot be focused).
confirmed.repro: bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t/t10.ts (browser baseline: log stays empty). Sift path, by reading: form [Save(disabled until valid)][Cancel/Delete (plain <button>, so type=submit)] -> Enter in a Sift field -> proxy.submit clicks Cancel/Delete. SPA login form with no submit button and no submit handler -> requestSubmit -> native GET to the current URL with the named fields (password included) in the query string.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The new default-button logic re-implements implicit submission without the 'disabled default button' and 'fields that block implicit submission' rules.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Take the first submit button in tree order; if it is disabled, do nothing. If there is no submit button and the form has more than one text-like field, fall back to key(field, 'Enter') instead of requestSubmit. Skip checkValidity when form.noValidate or the submitter has formNoValidate. Run the same validity check (and show the message) before the button path when the button is a submit button of the form.
confirmed.verdict: Ran t10.ts as a Chrome baseline. Enter in a form with <button disabled>Save</button><button>Delete</button> does not submit. Enter in a form with two text fields and no submit button does not submit either. Then bundled the real src/content/proxy.ts with bun and ran it in Chrome (scratchpad/v/t2v.ts). proxy.submit(field, null, f1) logged 'del clicked' and 'f1 submit by del', so it clicks Delete. For a novalidate form with an empty required field, it returned 'Please fill out this field.' and did not submit, while the browser would submit and let the site validate. Code at proxy.ts:174-195 confirms the requestSubmit fallback with no check for fields that block implicit submission, and that the button path skips the validity check.
confirmed.fix: Follow the implicit submission rules. Take the first submit button in tree order, even when disabled. If it is disabled, do nothing. If there is no submit button and more than one field blocks implicit submission, send Enter to the field instead of calling requestSubmit. Skip checkValidity when form.noValidate is set. On the button path, check validity unless the form has novalidate or the button has formNoValidate, and return the message.

confirmed.title: Portal keyboard navigation: Shift+Tab trap and no Escape for video portals, wrong exit for iframe portals, broken for shadow-DOM players
confirmed.evidence: Video boxes have no tabIndex (`tabIndex={b.media ? undefined : 0}`), so `box.focus()` is a no-op. Shift+Tab with `at <= 0` calls `e.preventDefault()` then `box.focus()` -> focus never moves (trap). Escape does nothing for videos. `at < 0` (focus on the portal root or a tabindex=-1 container, which is where a click on a player puts focus) counts as 'leaving', so forward Tab jumps to list[0] (the skip link at the top) instead of entering the controls. onPortalKey uses `e.target`, which at window is retargeted to the outermost shadow host, while portalOf uses path[0]; in a web-component player `at` is always -1. For iframe portals (maps, embeds, payment fields: the main 'other' kind), enterPortal focuses the iframe; keys then go to the frame's document, which Sift never sees (all_frames: false), so Escape cannot leave, and Tab out lands on Sift's first focusable, not after the box. enterPortal also picks a FOCUSABLE match without a visibility check.

confirmed.suggestedFix: Give media boxes tabIndex=-1 (or compute the previous/next Sift focusable by document position when the box is not focusable). Use composedPath()[0] in onPortalKey and search inside shadow roots. Treat at<0 as 'go to the first inside' for forward Tab when inside is non-empty. For iframe portals, catch focus returning to the top document (focusin on Sift after the iframe had focus) to place focus after the box, and say in the box label that Tab leaves.
confirmed.verdict: Read app.tsx:301-313 (video boxes get tabIndex undefined) and index.ts:209-226 and 651-656. For a video portal, Shift+Tab with at<=0 calls preventDefault and then box.focus(), which does nothing on a div without tabindex, so focus is trapped. Escape also does nothing. at<0 (focus on #movie_player-style tabindex=-1 roots) counts as leaving, so forward Tab goes to list[0], the skip button, because the box is not in siftFocusables. e.target at window is the retargeted shadow host, while portalOf uses path[0]. For iframe portals, enterPortal focuses the iframe. With all_frames:false (static/manifest.json), keys in a cross-origin frame never reach Sift, so Escape cannot leave.
confirmed.fix: Give video boxes tabIndex=-1 so box.focus() works. Compute at from e.composedPath()[0], and treat at<0 on forward Tab as entering the first control. Put a focus sentinel right after each iframe box so Tab out lands after the box. Filter enterPortal candidates with checkVisibility().

Inferred from the code and the library source, not run end to end.

confirmed.title: Rich-editor flush steals focus from Sift's textarea every 700 ms pause, breaking IME composition
confirmed.evidence: H.input arms a 700 ms timer on every input event, including input events during IME composition. flushEdits -> setEditable focuses the original editor (`el.focus()`) and later refocuses Sift's textarea. Verified (t4.ts) that moving focus fires the textarea's change synchronously ('change sync? active=' logged between 'before focus' and 'after focus'), so focus really leaves the field. Blurring a field during composition commits or cancels it (known Chrome behavior, not tested here).
confirmed.repro: Inferred: type Japanese/Chinese in a Sift field mirrored from a contenteditable (Gmail compose, chat box) and pause over 700 ms on the candidate list -> the composition is cut off.

confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:552-559: H.input re-arms a 700 ms flush on every input event, with no isComposing check. flushEdits calls setEditable, which calls el.focus() on the page editor and later back.focus() (proxy.ts:410-448). Ran t4.ts: moving focus away from an edited textarea fires its change event synchronously, so focus really leaves Sift's field on every 700 ms pause. Chrome commits or ends an active IME composition on blur. That part is known behavior and was not tested here.
confirmed.fix: Skip arming the timer while composing (check e.isComposing in onInput) and flush on compositionend. Better, never steal focus on a timer: flush only on blur or before an action.

confirmed.title: Shield toggling during rich-editor flush is recorded as 'recent' page changes, so findPopup can invent a popup or toast

'inert' is now in the observer's attributeFilter. afterAct() -> armRecent() runs before the observer callback (microtask after the click handler), so noteMutations records all those elements as recently changed. findPopup/findToast then climb from them to any fixed/absolute ancestor of popup size.

confirmed.suggestedFix: In noteMutations, ignore attribute records for 'inert' (and for elements carrying data-sift-inert / data-sift-portal), or call mo.takeRecords() right after withoutShield's two apply() calls and drop them.
confirmed.verdict: Bundled the real shield.ts, recent.ts, proxy.ts and extract/generic.ts with bun and ran them in Chrome (scratchpad/v/t11v.ts). The page had a fixed header with links, a contenteditable, a Post button and a fixed chat aside. The observer used Sift's attributeFilter. Steps: shieldOn([]), then proxy.setValue(editor), proxy.click(post), armRecent(), as H.act does. recentNodes() then held body, header#hdr, aside#chat, h1, p and button#post from the inert flips. findDialog() returned key 'pop:r5', the fixed header, as a popup dialog with its nav links. Before the action, findDialog was null.
confirmed.fix: Ignore attribute records for 'inert' (and Sift's own role demotion) in noteMutations. Or call mo.takeRecords() inside withoutShield and drop those records.

confirmed.title: Page wheel handlers still see Sift's wheel events (Lenis blocks scrolling of Sift); click is still visible to capture-phase outside-click hooks
confirmed.evidence: The stop list covers pointer, mouse, touch and focus events but not wheel or click. Checked the Lenis 1.1.13 source (unpkg): wrapper/eventsTarget default to window, wheel listener with passive:false, and `s.preventDefault()` unless the composed path has data-lenis-prevent; so on Lenis sites wheel over Sift is cancelled and the hidden page scrolls instead. From memory, not verified: VueUse onClickOutside listens to click on window with capture:true, so a click on Sift's copy of a dropdown closes the page dropdown before Sift replays the item click.
confirmed.repro: Lenis: curl https://unpkg.com/lenis@1.1.13/dist/lenis.mjs and grep 'addEventListener("wheel"' and 'preventDefault'. Any Lenis-based marketing site in Sift: mouse wheel does not scroll Sift.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add 'wheel' and 'touchmove' to the window-capture stop list as passive listeners (stopImmediatePropagation works in passive listeners, so no scroll jank). For click, consider handling Sift's activation in the window-capture click listener so page capture hooks run after Sift has acted.
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:175-183: 'wheel' is not in the stop list. Fetched lenis@1.1.13 from unpkg. The defaults are wrapper=window, eventsTarget=window and smoothWheel=true, with addEventListener('wheel', ..., {passive:false}). onVirtualScroll slices the composed path at the root element, and checks only data-lenis-prevent and the .lenis classes. sift-root has neither, so it calls preventDefault. On Lenis sites, wheel over Sift is cancelled and the hidden page scrolls instead. The click and outside-click part (VueUse) was not verified, and click cannot be stopped at window capture without breaking Sift's own handlers.
confirmed.fix: Add 'wheel' to the window-capture stop list for events whose path includes host. Register that listener as passive so scrolling stays fast; stopping propagation does not cancel Sift's own scrolling.

confirmed.title: Articles longer than 60,000 characters are cut before condensing, and the Short version does not say so
confirmed.evidence: const text = blocksText(a.blocks).slice(0, 60000); Everything after character 60,000 (about 9-10k English words) is never sent. The result is still labeled the article's 'Short version' and shown by default. It drops the end of long reads: conclusions, corrections, caveats.

confirmed.verdict: Read ai.ts:147: const text = blocksText(a.blocks).slice(0, 60000). Grepped src/content for 60000, truncat and similar words. There is no notice anywhere. ArticleView (app.tsx:321-336) shows the Short version by default with only the shortVersion tag. Any article over 60k characters is condensed from its first 60k only. One nuance from index.ts:297: at 60k chars the output cap is 8000 tokens. At the benchmark's 67% length ratio the output would be about 8k tokens, so some of these calls end in a Truncated error with no short version, which is harmless. When the model compresses more, the short version silently leaves out the end of the article.
confirmed.fix: When the text is cut, either chunk-condense the rest, or send a 'truncated' flag and show a line under the Short version such as 'Covers the first part of the article. Show full text for the rest.'

confirmed.title: Possible: the condense output budget is too small for scripts such as Devanagari, so every visit pays for a truncated call and caches nothing (unverified)
confirmed.evidence: maxTokens = 300 + chars/4 unless the text is CJK, kana, Hangul or Thai. Scripts such as Devanagari, Bengali or Tamil usually tokenize at fewer than 4 characters per token. A condensed output at the benchmark's ~67% length can then exceed the budget. That throws Truncated, so there is no short version. The result is not cached (index.ts:306 is skipped), and ai.ts:157 blocks a retry only for the current page view, so every visit pays for the call again. I did not measure Qwen's or Gemini's tokenizer on these scripts.
confirmed.repro: Condense a 5,000-character Hindi article and check for the 'output limit reached' error in the port replies.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Base the budget on a per-script chars-per-token estimate (or on the input token count from a cheap tokenizer), and cache a 'truncated' marker per key so the call is not repeated on each visit.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The density check covers only CJK and Thai.
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:288-297: the dense check covers only kana, CJK, Hangul and Thai. Everything else gets maxTokens = 300 + chars/4. Measured with the Qwen3 tokenizer (Qwen/Qwen3-8B tokenizer.json, the closest public tokenizer to the qwen/qwen3.8-27b condense model) on Wikipedia text, using /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/skeptic/tok.py. English: 4.9 chars/token. Hindi: 1.06 chars/token. Tamil: 0.91 chars/token. For 5,000 chars of Hindi the budget is 1,550 tokens, but output at the benchmark's 67% length is about 3,160 tokens (2.0x the budget). Tamil is 2.4x, and at 20k chars 2.4x and 2.8x. That ends in finish_reason length, then Truncated. withFallback rethrows Truncated without trying the fallback (index.ts:192), nothing is cached (:306), and ai.ts:157 blocks retries only for this page view. So Hindi and Tamil articles basically never get a short version, and every visit pays for a cut-off call. Caveat: qwen3.8's exact tokenizer could differ from Qwen3's.
confirmed.fix: Estimate tokens by script, not one global ratio. For example, count characters outside Latin, Cyrillic and Greek as about 1 token each (estTokens = latinChars/4 + otherChars), and keep the 8000 cap.

confirmed.evidence: `title = allText.split(/\n/)[0]` uses allText = textIn(el), and clean() has collapsed all whitespace, so the split returns the whole card text.
confirmed.repro: A detected item member with no heading and no link (up to 40% of members are allowed): the title is the whole card text cut at 197 chars, and every meta piece is then skipped as already inside the title.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Expose a lines reader (rawText split on \n, each cleaned) and use its first non-empty line.
confirmed.verdict: Ran in Chrome (c19.ts). A detected item member with no heading and no link got as its title the whole card text: 'Gift card Give the gift of choice … From 10 dollars', and meta []. clean() in textIn collapses newlines, so allText.split(/\n/) at line 727 never splits.
confirmed.fix: Use the first text group from the tree walk (the first block's text) as the title, or rawText(el).split('\n') before clean. Then cap it at about 120 chars.

confirmed.title: Byline-token skip is page-wide
confirmed.evidence: Once ctx.hasByline is set, every element with author/authors/published/timestamp tokens and under 300 chars is skipped anywhere on the page.
confirmed.repro:
On an article page, comment authors (`.comment-author`), quote attributions (`

— Shakespeare

` inside the article) and authors in related lists disappear.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Skip only inside the article header region: before the first article paragraph, or a sibling of or near the title h1, and not inside comments.
confirmed.verdict:
Ran in Chrome (c20.ts) with meta author and published_time, so hasByline is true. Inside the article,

— William Shakespeare

was dropped. In the comments section, both div.comment-author names (Ana López, Bo Smith) were dropped, and only the comment texts remained. The line 919 check is page-wide.
confirmed.fix: Skip byline-token elements only when they are before the article body or in its header area: outside ctx.articleEl, or within the first few blocks of it, and not inside a comments section or blockquote/figure. Better, skip only the specific element that byline() read.

confirmed.title: Icon-ligature filter also removes digit-only text in icon-classed elements
confirmed.evidence: `/^\s*[a-z0-9_]+\s*$/` accepts "3" or "17", and ICON_CLASS matches any icon/icons token.
confirmed.repro: A cart or notification badge `3` or `4` loses its number.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Require a leading letter: /^\s*[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\s*$/.
confirmed.verdict: Ran in Chrome (c21.ts). textIn(Cart 3) gave 'Cart', and the 'Rating 4' link gave 'Rating'. findTop's Cart action lost its count. ICON_CLASS matches 'icon-badge', and /^\s*[a-z0-9_]+\s*$/ accepts digits.
confirmed.fix: Require a letter in the ligature test (/^\s*[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\s*$/), since icon ligature names start with a letter. Also skip it when the class has badge/count/counter tokens.

confirmed.title: Silent truncation and budget leaks
confirmed.where: src/content/extract/generic.ts:1214 (300 rows), 1071 and 1385/1407 (ctx spread copies count)
confirmed.evidence: `body.slice(0, 300)` drops rows 301+ with no marker. `{ ...ctx, inArticle: false }` copies count by value, so the comment sub-walk gets its own 25000 budget on top of the parent's.
confirmed.repro: A 1000-row data table shows 300 rows with no 'more' indication. A huge comments section can push total visits well past BUDGET.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a 'N more rows' notice or a collapsed section. Share the counter through an object (ctx.budget = {n}) instead of a number.
confirmed.verdict: Read code. table() line 1214 slices body rows to 300, and the pushed table block has no marker or count of the remaining rows. At line 1071, { ...ctx, inArticle: false } copies count by value. The comments sub-walk increments its own copy and the parent's ctx.count does not advance, so total visits can exceed BUDGET. I did not run a timing repro for this.
confirmed.fix: Add a 'more rows' indicator (rows total, or a 'Show all N rows' action) when slicing. Pass count through by reference (keep a shared budget object in ctx), or copy sub.count back into ctx.count after the sub-walk.

confirmed.title: outsideSurfaces lifts maps from footers or rails to the top of the page
confirmed.evidence: It takes any SURFACE_SEL outside scope that is not an ad, ignoring footer/aside/chrome and noise ancestors, and pushes it before all content.
confirmed.repro: An article page with a 'Find our store' Leaflet map in the site footer: the map portal appears first, above the article.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Skip surfaces whose ancestors are chrome or noise per isChrome/NOISE_TOKEN, or only take them when scope === root or the surface is larger than the scope.
confirmed.verdict: Ran in Chrome (c24.ts). An article page with a footer > div.leaflet-container (400x250) gave blocks ['portal','h','article'], with the footer map first. A non-article main page gave the same: ['portal','h','p']. outsideSurfaces (1589-1602) ignores footer, aside and chrome ancestors, and walkPage pushes its results before the content.
confirmed.fix: In outsideSurfaces, skip surfaces inside footer, aside, contentinfo, complementary or chrome (isChrome ancestors). Only lift a surface outside scope when it is large (for example over 30% of the viewport) and near the scope, and place it after the content unless it comes before the scope in document order.

confirmed.title: Page-world key helper dispatches on the shadow host instead of the real target
confirmed.evidence: `const target = e.target as Element;` in a document capture listener: for an event dispatched inside a shadow root, e.target at document is the retargeted host. The KeyboardEvent is then dispatched on the host, so listeners on the inner input or dialog never get Enter/Escape.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning (standard event retargeting): a search input inside a web component's shadow root with no <form> -> H.submit -> key(field, 'Enter') -> Enter arrives at the host; the component's input keydown handler does not run.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Use `const target = e.composedPath()[0] as Element;`.
confirmed.verdict: Read src/main/index.ts:195-207. The document capture listener takes e.target, which for a composed event dispatched inside a shadow root is retargeted to the shadow host. KeyboardEvents dispatched on the host never reach listeners on the inner input. proxy.key dispatches sift-key with composed:true on the field (proxy.ts:455-458), so H.submit sending Enter to a field in a shadow root (no form) misses the field's own handler.
confirmed.fix: Use e.composedPath()[0] as the dispatch target in main/index.ts.

confirmed.title: The 'focus falls out of Sift' handler is dead code after the capture-phase fix
confirmed.evidence: focusout is in the window-capture list and is stopped with stopImmediatePropagation when the path includes host, so the host's focusout listener never runs. Verified (t1.ts): 'hostFocusoutFired': 0. After a Sift dialog or menu closes, focus stays on body until the next key.
confirmed.repro: bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/t/t1.ts
confirmed.suggestedFix: Move the restore logic into the window-capture listener for type 'focusout' (before stopping), and return focus to the control that opened the dialog rather than main.
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:175-193. focusout is in the window-capture list and gets stopImmediatePropagation whenever the path includes host, so the host-level focusout listener can never run. Ran t1.ts: hostFocusoutFired = 0. The effect is small: the body-key branch moves focus back to main on the next key.
confirmed.fix: Move the refocus logic into the window-capture focusout listener before stopping the event, or delete the dead handler.

confirmed.title: Key guard swallows untrusted key events aimed at body, including Sift's own Escape
confirmed.evidence: The body branch stops every keydown/keyup/keypress whose target is body, trusted or not. closeDialog falls back to `proxy.key(target ?? pageFocus ?? document.body, "Escape")` when the dialog element is gone, and that synthetic Escape is then stopped by Sift's own guard before page listeners see it. Page scripts that dispatch synthetic key events on body or document are also blocked.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: dialog element removed, Sift sheet Close pressed with no close button -> Escape dispatched on body -> stopped at window capture.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Start the guard with `if (!e.isTrusted) return;` (after the Alt+Shift+S check).
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:145-156 and 627-634. The body branch stops every keydown, keyup and keypress whose path[0] is body, trusted or not. In closeDialog, when the dialog element is gone, pageFocus is null because activeElement is host. So proxy.key(document.body,'Escape') runs, and its event (also the one the main-world helper re-dispatches on body) is stopped at window capture before any page listener. Narrow trigger: it needs the dialog element to be disconnected.
confirmed.fix: In the body branch, return early for untrusted events (!e.isTrusted), or mark Sift's own synthetic events and let them through.

confirmed.title: Mouse wheel over a video blocks Ctrl+wheel page zoom
confirmed.evidence: onWheel calls `e.preventDefault()` for every wheel over a shown video, including ctrlKey wheels (Ctrl+scroll and trackpad pinch), which cancels Chrome's zoom. This matters for low-vision users.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: in Sift, put the pointer over a playing video and press Ctrl+scroll -> Sift scrolls, zoom does not change.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Return early when e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey.
confirmed.verdict: Read portal.ts:64-73. onWheel is registered with passive:false and calls preventDefault for every wheel over a shown video, with no ctrlKey check. In Chrome, cancelling a ctrlKey wheel (Ctrl+scroll, trackpad pinch) blocks page zoom, so zoom does not work while the pointer is over a video.
confirmed.fix: In onWheel, return early when e.ctrlKey or e.metaKey is set.

confirmed.title: Portals cover Sift's sheet Close button and the bottom-right switch
confirmed.evidence: Inside a dialog the clip top is the sheet's own top (`top = r.top`), ignoring the sticky .sheet-head. A portal scrolled up in the sheet paints over the Close button and takes its clicks. In the main view nothing clips the fixed .toggle (styles.ts:148), so a portal near the bottom-right covers the switch.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: dialog with a video or iframe, scroll the sheet so the portal reaches the top -> Close is under the portal.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Use max(sheet.top, .sheet-head.bottom) as the top clip. Make the switch its own top-layer popover that is raised after the portals, or cut its rectangle out with a clip-path polygon.
confirmed.verdict: Read portal.ts:225-241 and styles.ts:143 and 148. Inside a sheet, the clip top is the sheet's own top, but .sheet-head is position:sticky. Portals sit in the top layer above sift-root, so a portal scrolled up inside the sheet paints over the Close button and takes its clicks. In the main view, the clip runs to innerHeight and ignores the fixed .toggle at bottom-right, so a portal under that corner covers the switch.
confirmed.fix: In clipBounds for a sheet, use the .sheet-head's bottom as the top. Also clip the portal away from the toggle's rect, or keep its bottom above the toggle when they overlap.

confirmed.title: Suspended portals are only clipped, so they stay focusable and visible to screen readers
confirmed.evidence: Suspension sets `clip-path: inset(50%)` and keeps `visibility: visible`. Sift's menu and dialog do not trap focus, so Tab past the sheet's last control can land inside an invisible player or iframe.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: open Sift's menu on a page with a video, Tab past the last menu link.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Also set visibility: hidden (or inert) while suspended.
confirmed.verdict: Read portal.ts:281-286: suspension only sets clip-path inset(50%) while visibility stays visible. The portal path is kept out of inert by the shield, and Menu and DialogView have no focus trap (app.tsx:471-510), so its controls stay in the tab order (they come before sift-root in document order) and in the accessibility tree while hidden.
confirmed.fix: While suspended, also set visibility:hidden (or inert on the portal element), and restore it when resumed.

confirmed.title: Validation and toast notices: never cleared, off-screen when scrolled, announced twice
confirmed.evidence: H.submit sets store.notice with no timeout, and nothing clears it on success or in checkUrl, so a stale 'Email: Please fill out this field' stays across SPA pages. The notice renders at the top of <main>, so after submitting at the bottom of a long form or clicking Add to cart far down a list, sighted users never see it. The text goes into two live regions (the notice p role=status and the .sr role=status div), so screen readers read it twice; a repeat of the same toast does not change .sr and is not read again.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: submit an invalid long form from the bottom; fix it and submit; navigate within the SPA -> the old warning is still there.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Clear store.notice in checkUrl and after the next successful act/submit, show notices in a fixed spot, keep role=status on one element only, and clear announce before setting the same text again.
confirmed.verdict:
Read index.ts:291-308, 379-395 and 586-591, and app.tsx:552 and 563. The validation notice from H.submit has no timeout. A later successful submit, checkUrl (SPA navigation) and updateToast (which clears only its own toast) never clear it. .notice is not sticky or fixed (styles.ts:128) and renders at the top of
, so it is off-screen after submitting at the bottom. The same text goes to the

and the .sr live region. The double announcement depends on the screen reader, since a newly inserted live region is often not read.
confirmed.fix: Clear store.notice on a successful submit, in checkUrl, and when the field changes. Show it in a fixed or sticky spot, or scroll it into view. Announce it through one live region only.

confirmed.title: A dismissed dialog that cannot be closed comes back whenever another dialog becomes current
confirmed.evidence: `for (const k of store.dismissed) if (k !== page.dialog?.key) store.dismissed.delete(k);` drops a dismissed key as soon as a different dialog (a menu the user opened) is current, even though the dismissed one is still open on the page.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning: dismiss a role=dialog chat widget that ignores Escape and has no close button; open and close any page menu through Sift -> the widget sheet is back.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Delete a dismissed key only when its dialog element is gone or not visible (check elOf(ref) and visibility), not when it is merely not the current dialog.
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:349 and generic.ts:1374-1438. A dismissed key is dropped as soon as page.dialog has a different key, even if the dismissed dialog is still open. Narrower than claimed: findDialog returns role=dialog, alertdialog and aria-modal candidates before the popup and menu branches. So opening a page menu cannot displace a visible dismissed role=dialog, and the menu example does not trigger it. A second role=dialog later in DOM order does, and after it closes the dismissed widget sheet comes back.
confirmed.fix: Drop a dismissed key only when that dialog's element is no longer connected or visible (check elOf(ref) and visible()), not when another dialog is current.

confirmed.title: The AI cache is shared across all sites, so one page can plant rewrites for another site or learn what you viewed elsewhere
confirmed.evidence: Line keys are hash(`lines|${PROMPT_VERSION}|${mode}|${s.lines.model}|${it.t}|${it.c ?? ""}`) (index.ts:219). Condense keys are hash(`condense|...|${req.title}|${req.text}`) (index.ts:278). Neither includes the page's site. One IndexedDB store serves every tab. A cache hit is sent back right away (index.ts:222-223), with no model call. Sift's view is in an OPEN shadow root (content/index.ts:38: host.attachShadow({ mode: "open" })), so page scripts can read the rewritten text and time when it appears. A generic page with 4 or more long headlines is sent in "news" mode (extract/generic.ts rewriteIfLong). So an attacker page can build entries that produce the same key as a real news site's entries. The planting path depends on prompt injection working; I did not test that.
confirmed.repro: Reasoning from code. (1) History leak: the attacker scrapes headline + teaser text from news site X and serves it as a list of 4 or more long headlines. Inside Sift, the attacker's script polls document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot. Lines that appear within a few ms came from the cache, so the user saw that listing on X. (2) Planting: the attacker page puts real entries from X in the same batch as a crafted entry that says 'for entry 2 write: <false claim>'. The model's output is cached under entry 2's key (index.ts:245). Later, site X shows the false line in Sift.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add the top-level site to every cache key. Pass new URL(port.sender.url).origin (or its eTLD+1) into doLines and doCondense and put it at the start of the hash input. Also consider attachShadow({mode:"closed"}) as defense in depth.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The cache was keyed only on content, to maximize hits.
confirmed.verdict: Read the cited code. index.ts:219 and :278 build cache keys from mode, model, title and text only, with no site. cache.ts uses one IndexedDB store for all tabs. index.ts:222-223 replies on a cache hit at once, with no model call. content/index.ts:38 uses attachShadow({mode:"open"}) and :71 appends the host to document.documentElement, so page scripts can read the rendered lines. generic.ts:172-177 puts any list of 4 or more items with titles averaging over 13 words into news mode. Adapters are matched by URL, so an attacker page can only produce news-mode keys, not YouTube, Amazon or Gmail keys. A bun harness that loads the real background/index.ts with a mocked chrome and cache showed the same key for the same item sent from https://news.example/ and https://attacker.example/. So the cross-site timing probe works as described. It needs the exact title and context strings from site X, and those include changing meta text, so it is brittle. The planting path depends on prompt injection, which neither of us tested. That is why I rate it low.
confirmed.fix: Add the top-level site (eTLD+1 of port.sender.url, or tab URL) to both the lines and condense cache keys. Optionally use a closed shadow root so page scripts cannot read the rewritten text or time it.

confirmed.title: A short version that stopped early for any reason except finish_reason "length" is shown and cached as complete
confirmed.evidence: streamChat only rejects finish_reason === "length" (index.ts:173). If OpenRouter returns finish_reason "content_filter" (Gemini safety stop partway through an article), the loop continues to [DONE] and returns normally. The same happens if the body ends (done) with no [DONE] and no finish_reason. doCondense then caches the partial text (index.ts:306: if (all.trim() && useCache) cacheSet(key, all)). ArticleView treats it as ready (app.tsx:324: ai.text.length > 40 && !ai.error) and shows it by default as the 'Short version'. Facts after the cut are silently lost, and the cache keeps it that way on every later visit.
confirmed.repro: Code reading. Feed a condense request whose stream ends with a chunk {choices:[{delta:{},finish_reason:"content_filter"}]} then data: [DONE]. withFallback resolves, cacheSet runs, and the UI shows the partial text with no error.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In streamChat, record the last finish_reason. Return successfully only when it is "stop" (or [DONE] came after a "stop"). Throw Truncated for "length", "content_filter" or "error", and when the stream ends with no finish_reason.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The truncation check covered only the output-limit case.
confirmed.verdict: Ran a bun test in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/skeptic/bg.test.ts. It imports the real src/background/index.ts with a mocked chrome, mocked fetch (SSE) and a mocked cache module. Stream with content plus finish_reason "content_filter" plus [DONE]: replies were delta then done, with no error, and cacheSet ran once. Stream that closed cleanly with no [DONE] and no finish_reason: the same result, done and cached. finish_reason "length": an error, not cached. app.tsx:324 treats any text over 40 chars with no error as ready, and it is shown by default. Rated low because the main condense model is Qwen on Cerebras, which does not normally emit content_filter. Gemini is only the fallback, and clean early closes are rare.
confirmed.fix: In streamChat, track the last finish_reason. Treat anything other than "stop" (content_filter, error, or a body that ends with no [DONE] and no finish_reason) as incomplete: throw, so doCondense never caches it and the UI keeps the full text.

confirmed.title: Saving Options once freezes all four model IDs and their extra fields, so default model changes never reach that user
confirmed.evidence: Options saves { ...s, neverSift }, where s = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...saved }. That includes lines, linesFallback, condense and condenseFallback. loadSettings replaces a model config with the default only when its .model is empty (index.ts:18-20). The published zip has no key, so every public user must click Save to enter one. From then on they are pinned to the 2026-10-24 model choices. If a model is retired, the main and fallback models both fail, and AI stays broken: errors, then a 30 s pause, then repeat.
confirmed.repro: Save Options once, change DEFAULT_SETTINGS.lines.model, rebuild and reload. The worker still uses the old model from storage.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Save only the fields that differ from the defaults. For example, store model overrides as empty strings meaning 'use the default', and in Options compare each field with DEFAULT_SETTINGS before saving.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The merged settings object is saved as a whole.
confirmed.verdict: Read options/index.tsx:15-16 and :40. The page merges {...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, ...saved} and saves {...s, neverSift}, which writes lines, linesFallback, condense and condenseFallback in full. Grepped src: Options is the only writer of 'settings'. loadSettings (index.ts:17-20) falls back to defaults only when .model is empty. deploy.sh removes local-key.json, so public users must Save to enter a key, and that pins them to today's models and extra fields. The risk is real because condense uses provider only:["cerebras"] with allow_fallbacks:false, and Cerebras retires models often. It only shows up when defaults change.
confirmed.fix: Save only the fields that differ from DEFAULT_SETTINGS (or only the fields the user edited). Or store an 'models follow defaults' flag and ignore a saved model config that equals an older default.

confirmed.title: The one-line cache key leaves out the language, so a line in one language can be shown on a page in another
confirmed.evidence: The key is mode|model|title|context. The prompt's lang comes from detectLang(title, req.lang) (line 231). For short titles detection is unreliable, so lang falls back to the page language. The same title and context on an English page and a Spanish page share one cache entry. The second page gets the first page's language, which breaks 'keeps the page's language'.
confirmed.repro: View an item with an identical short title and context first on an en page, then on an es page. The es page gets the cached English line.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add the detected lang (the value sent in input[i].lang) to the hash. Compute detectLang before the keys.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The key was written before per-entry lang was added to the prompt.
confirmed.verdict: Read index.ts:219 (key = lines|PROMPT_VERSION|mode|model|t|c) and :231 (prompt lang = detectLang(title, req.lang), which falls back to the page lang when detection is unreliable). The bun harness sent the same item {t:"Messi", c:""} with lang en and then lang es. Both got key 7892b06378034ef5c3beaccc0c380f76. It matters only when detection fails, which means short titles, and when title and context match exactly across pages in different languages. YouTube and Amazon context is usually localized, and news titles are long enough to detect. The prompt also keeps short plain titles almost as is. So visible harm is rare, but the mismatch is real.
confirmed.fix: Add the resolved per-item lang (the value detectLang returns) to the key. Compute it before the cache lookup.

confirmed.title: The deploy key-leak guard can miss a match under pipefail, and dist always contains the key
confirmed.evidence: With set -o pipefail, `if unzip -l zip | grep -q local-key` fails when grep -q exits early and unzip then gets SIGPIPE (exit 141). The guard then passes even though it matched. The listing is about 1 KB today, written in one stdio flush, so the guard works now. It breaks once the listing grows past the stdio buffer. The check also matches only the file name, not the key text. build.ts:22 copies local-key.json into dist on every build, so any other packaging of dist (Chrome 'Pack extension', a store upload) ships the key. I verified the published /var/www/sift.pujia.ar/sift.zip: no local-key.json entry, and the key string is in none of its files.
confirmed.repro: bash -o pipefail -c 'if seq 1 200000 | grep -q 1; then echo found; else echo missed; fi' prints 'missed'.
confirmed.suggestedFix: list=$(unzip -Z1 "$tmp/sift.zip"); if grep -q local-key <<<"$list"; then ...; fi. Also scan the unzipped files for the key's prefix (grep -r 'sk-or-'). Better still, have build.ts skip the key copy for a release build (for example a --release flag that deploy.sh passes).
confirmed.suspectedCause: A common pipefail + grep -q pitfall.
confirmed.verdict: Tested in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/skeptic/ziptest with python3 -m zipfile and unzip -l under bash -o pipefail. A zip with 3,000 files and a-local-key.json listed 5th (143 KB listing) printed 'missed' 3 of 3 times. The same zip with local-key.json listed near the end printed 'found'. A small zip like today's dist printed found-small. The published listing is 878 bytes, so the guard works today. It is a second check after rm -f at deploy.sh:10, so this is a latent bug in a backup check. dist containing local-key.json is by design for dev installs (build.ts comment), not a defect.
confirmed.fix: Avoid grep -q in a pipefail pipeline: listing=$(unzip -Z1 "$tmp/sift.zip"); if grep -q local-key <<<"$listing"; then ... Also check that the key value itself is absent: if unzip -p "$tmp/sift.zip" | grep -qF "$(jq -r .apiKey local-key.json)"; then fail (capture the output first for the same reason).

rejected.title: No 'Message sent' confirmation after a reply in Sift
rejected.why: Reproduced only on the synthetic stand-in, after a fresh load of fx/gmail#inbox/2: #reply reads 'Message sent', window.__sent has the body, Sift's main lacks 'Message sent', and the live region is empty. But the stand-in writes the status inline into the thread (#reply div.vh), which real Gmail does not do. Real Gmail shows a fixed bottom toast, and Sift has a separate toast path for that (findToast in generic.ts, then store.notice/announce in index.ts). I cannot test real Gmail (no sign-in), so there is no evidence that real users miss the confirmation. This is a stand-in artifact until shown on real Gmail.

rejected.title: After exiting full screen, Sift briefly loses Sign in and Subscribe/Like/Dislike/Save
rejected.why: I could not reproduce the claimed 5-second loss or the missing Sign in. Twice I clicked Full screen, then document.exitFullscreen(), and sampled Sift's buttons. At 0 ms and about 500 ms after exit: 'Sign in, Save to playlist' (Sign in present). By about 800 ms: 'Sign in, Subscribe, Like 19M, Dislike, Save', which matched the original and stayed. At 1.5 s and 6.5 s everything was present (screenshot T2-yt-after-fs.png). A stale render under a second while YouTube moves its layout back is within Sift's normal re-extract delay, not a lasting sync failure.

rejected.title: Daily Mail video article: lead video shown twice, title repeated, player internals leak (snapshot)
rejected.why: Not confirmable as a product defect. I reproduced the outline on the snapshot: the poster img, then the portal, then 'play video', 'video progress bar', 'Current Time 0:00', 'Video Quality…', and the caption-settings selects. But the snapshot has scripts stripped and lacks video.js CSS, so vjs-hidden settings render. The poster is never swapped for the player, and Sift's Play has no script to drive. The live page (dailymail.com article-16233447) returns 'Access Denied' (Akamai) from this IP, so the live behavior is unknown. The title repeated as H2 is the same defect as finding 15 (confirmed live on BBC), and the duplicate poster is covered by finding 16.

rejected.title: Map portals take the mouse wheel, so scrolling with the pointer over the map zooms it instead of scrolling Sift
rejected.why: The behavior is real: a trusted wheel (deltaY 300) at (600,400) over the Maps portal changed 17z→16z, and the same wheel at x=100 scrolled Sift's host (scrollTop 300). portal.ts onWheel only redirects wheel for video portals. But this is the map's own working surface, the same as on the original page, and the product goal is to keep tool surfaces usable inside Sift. Wheel zoom is also the only mouse zoom left (finding 7). The gutters and the keyboard still scroll Sift. This is a design trade-off, not a defect against the stated goals.

rejected.title: Test harness: SIFT_TAB=n can address a different window between runs
rejected.why: This is a harness issue, not a Sift defect, and I could not reproduce it. scripts/lib.ts tab() does pick pages()[n] by index and creates windows when the list is short, so a closed or new tab could shift indexes. But in three listings over my whole session the order stayed the same, and every one of my SIFT_TAB=5 runs hit the same tab. puppeteer's order is not the /json/list recency order either. I did not open or close tabs to test it, because that would shift other testers' windows.

rejected.title: raise() can ping-pong with page or extension code that keeps its own popover on top
rejected.why: The parts are real: t9.ts shows hide-then-show fires one toggle with open->open, and the listener does raise() again for any non-modal open toggle. But the loop needs third-party page or extension code that re-raises its own popover on toggle events. The finding admits this is speculative, and no such code was found or shown. Not confirmed as a defect.

rejected.title: The API key in storage.local is readable from content scripts after each browser start, until the worker calls setAccessLevel
rejected.why: I could not confirm this in code or reproduce it without a browser. Read the test in /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/ext-test/run.ts. It calls browser.installExtension(dir/ext) on every run, so run 2 re-loads the unpacked extension. That is a reinstall or reload, not a plain browser restart, so it does not show the access level is lost across a normal restart. The 'read:{}' result in run 1 came at first install, when no secret existed yet. That matches Sift: at install there is no key in storage. Only Sift's own content script runs in that world, and it never reads storage, so only a compromised renderer could use the window. That is defense in depth, not a defect against the product goals. Storage.local is readable by content scripts by default in nearly every extension.

rejected.title: Counts can be recorded while they are off: the off-flag starts as true and is loaded asynchronously
rejected.why: The window exists in code: stats.ts:12 sets enabled=true until the async storage get at :15 resolves. The reporting agent's own 4 trials on Chrome 151 recorded nothing with counts off, and I have no repro that shows the race winning. Even if it did, flushStats (stats.ts:56) sends nothing while analytics is false. A few counts would only leave the browser if the user later turned counts back on. I cannot confirm that it happens, and the impact is negligible.

rejected.title: Incognito use is counted, saved to disk, and reported
rejected.why: Confirmed the facts. static/manifest.json has no 'incognito' key, so it runs in spanning mode. index.ts:363 bumps every 'stat' with no sender.tab.incognito check. But stats are per-day integer counters only (page, toOriginal, action, error, ms). They hold no URL, site or content. The incognito rule at index.ts:332 protects page text in the AI cache, which is browsing data. A daily page count is not. Running in incognito also needs the user to opt in. Nothing in the product goals or the privacy text is broken.
